title: Analytical data dictionary
text: This dictionary documents the record grain and the principal fields used in the analysis. It describes derived analytical data; record-level FIA observations are intentionally not distributed with the public repository.

title: Analytical data dictionary
text:
Record grain and keys
The analytical unit is one measured forest condition within one FIA plot visit. The composite key is plt_cn + condid. Tree and seedling records are aggregated to that grain before they are joined, preventing many-to-many row inflation.








Field
Type / unit
Definition




plt_cn
character identifier
FIA plot-visit control number. Used as a relational key; not a coordinate.


condid
integer identifier
Condition number within the plot visit.


geoid
five-character code
State and county FIPS code used for county-safe spatial joins and the county random intercept.


county_name
character
FIA county name resolved from the database reference table.


measyear
year
Calendar year of field measurement. Observations in this release span 2018–2025.


forest_type
character
Active type in FIA maple/beech/birch group 800 (codes 801, 802, 805, or 809), which this project uses as its operational northern-hardwood cohort.

text:
Sampling and stand context








Field
Type / unit
Definition and missing-value rule




condprop_unadj
proportion
Unadjusted plot-area share assigned to the condition. Retained for FIA area context; it is not used as a universal tree-frame denominator.


micrprop_unadj
proportion
Unadjusted share of microplot sampling assigned to the condition. A value greater than zero demonstrates seedling sampling opportunity.


subpprop_unadj
proportion
Unadjusted share of subplot sampling assigned to the condition; used for live trees measured on subplots.


macrprop_unadj
proportion
Unadjusted share of macroplot sampling assigned to the condition; used only when a populated macroplot breakpoint applies.


seedling_sampled
logical
TRUE only when micrprop_unadj > 0. An absent seedling record may become zero only under this condition.


stand_age
years
FIA stand-age estimate (STDAGE). Missing values remain missing and are never silently imputed.


disturbed
logical
TRUE when any of DSTRBCD1–DSTRBCD3 contains a positive disturbance code.


treated
logical
TRUE when any of TRTCD1–TRTCD3 contains a positive treatment code. Included as an observational primary-model covariate; it is not a causal management effect.

title: Analytical data dictionary
text:
Live-tree and size-class metrics
Live trees have STATUSCD = 1. Sugar maple is resolved from REF_SPECIES as Acer saccharum, FIA species code 318. For tree (i), the plot-basis basal-area contribution is
[ 0.005454 _i^2 _i. ]








Field
Unit
Definition




total_ba_ft2_ac
ft²/acre
Sum of frame-corrected live-tree contributions: microplot records divide by micrprop_unadj, subplot records by subpprop_unadj, and applicable macroplot records by macrprop_unadj.


maple_ba_ft2_ac
ft²/acre
Sugar-maple component of the frame-corrected live-tree density.


maple_sapling_ba_ft2_ac
ft²/acre
Frame-corrected basal area of live sugar-maple TREE records with DBH 1–4.9 inches.


maple_sapling_present
logical
TRUE when at least one live sugar-maple TREE record has DBH 1–4.9 inches. The primary model uses this intermediate-cohort indicator.


overstory_total_ba_ft2_ac
ft²/acre
Frame-corrected basal area of all live TREE records with DBH ≥ 5 inches.


established_maple_ba_ft2_ac
ft²/acre
Frame-corrected basal area of live sugar-maple TREE records with DBH ≥ 5 inches. This is the primary continuous maple exposure.


nonmaple_ba_ft2_ac
ft²/acre
total_ba_ft2_ac - maple_ba_ft2_ac, bounded below at zero.


maple_ba_share
proportion
Frame-corrected sugar-maple basal area divided by frame-corrected total live-tree basal area.


established_maple_ba_share
proportion
established_maple_ba_ft2_ac / overstory_total_ba_ft2_ac, with zero assigned when no live DBH ≥ 5-inch tree basal area is present. Used only for the descriptive gap screen.


established_maple_records
count
Number of live sugar-maple TREE records with DBH ≥ 5 inches. The primary cohort requires at least one.



The derived total is checked against FIA COND.BALIVE; the pipeline enforces strict correlation and absolute-error gates that detect use of a wrong sampling frame. Implementation: R/basal_area.R.

text:
Regeneration metrics and response








Field
Type / unit
Definition and interpretation




maple_seedling_tpa
trees/acre
Sugar-maple seedling TPA_UNADJ summed on the plot basis and divided by micrprop_unadj. NA when seedling sampling was not demonstrated.


maple_seedling_detected
0 / 1 / NA
1 when a sampled condition has positive sugar-maple seedling density; 0 when sampled but none were tallied; NA when sampling opportunity is unknown.


outcome_no_seedlings
0 / 1
Primary model response: 1 - maple_seedling_detected. It means “no seedlings tallied,” not confirmed ecological absence.


established_percentile
0–1
Sample percentile of established_maple_ba_share among conditions with usable seedling sampling.


regeneration_percentile
0–1
Sample percentile of log(1 + maple_seedling_tpa) among usable conditions.


potential_gap
logical
TRUE when established_maple_ba_share is at or above the sample upper-third threshold and no sugar-maple seedlings were tallied. Exploratory, not a validated ecological index.


potential_gap_sensitivity
logical
Alternative flag using the upper-quartile established-share threshold.



Implementation: R/regeneration.R and R/features.R.

Climate fields
Climate fields are 1991–2020 Daymet normals from the 1-km cell containing each Census Gazetteer county internal point. They are county-scale spatial proxies, not plot-level measurements or county-wide areal averages.








Field
Unit
Definition

°C
Mean across years of daily (tmin + tmax) / 2, averaged within year and then across 1991–2020.


mean_annual_precip_mm
mm/year
Mean annual sum of daily precipitation across 1991–2020.



Implementation: R/climate.R.

title: Analytical data dictionary
text:
Model transformations
Continuous predictors are standardized after defining the final model-complete cohort, so one standardized unit refers to the fitted 1,072-condition primary cohort. Basal-area predictors are transformed with log(1 + x) before standardization. The scaling means, standard deviations, transformations, and cohort size are published as a separate audit table.







Model field
Source and transformation




z_maple_ba
standardized log(1 + established_maple_ba_ft2_ac) in the primary model; retained as a linear term after functional-form comparison


maple_sapling_present
factor with FALSE as the reference level


z_nonmaple_ba
standardized log(1 + nonmaple_ba_ft2_ac)


z_microplot_coverage
standardized micrprop_unadj


treated
factor with FALSE as the reference level


z_stand_age
standardized stand_age


disturbed
factor with FALSE as the reference level


z_mean_temp
standardized mean_annual_temp_c


z_precip
standardized mean_annual_precip_mm


z_year
standardized measyear



The supported release model is a mixed-effects logistic regression with a county random intercept. It separates established-tree basal area from sugar-maple sapling presence and reports adjusted probability profiles by sapling state. Ten-fold internal grouped validation holds out whole counties, relearns transformations within each training fold, and predicts held-out counties with fixed effects only. Conventional coefficient inference is supplemented by Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted p-values and a county-cluster CR1 sensitivity analysis. Model construction and support gates are in R/models.R.
The contextual full-cohort baseline uses standardized log(1 + maple_ba_ft2_ac) with a three-degree-of-freedom natural spline. It is not the primary inferential model because the exposure combines saplings and established trees.

title: Analytical data dictionary
text:
Interpretation boundaries

TPA_UNADJ expands records within the plot design; it is not a statewide survey weight.
Zeros are assigned only when the relevant sampling opportunity is demonstrated.
Exact FIA plot locations are confidential. Public FIADB coordinates may be approximate; this analysis neither uses nor infers them, relying only on county identifiers.
Gap flags and fitted associations are exploratory and are not causal or design-based prevalence estimates.
The primary size classes are observed at one measurement; they do not estimate longitudinal transition probabilities.
County Wilson intervals are unweighted binomial reference intervals. They ignore FIA survey design and within-county clustering and are descriptive rather than inferential county estimates.

See Analysis decisions for the complete decision log.

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
Michigan · Northern hardwoods · 2025 current evaluation · measurements 2018–2025
Mature sugar maples do not guarantee the next generation.
In Michigan northern hardwoods where larger sugar-maple trees are already present, this study asks a simple question: what distinguishes places where survey crews recorded maple seedlings from places where they recorded none?

FIA relational data size-class ecology mixed-effects modeling county-held-out validation




The descriptive screen keeps positive tallies and true zeros visually distinct.

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
Abstract
This reproducible study examines 1,457 Michigan FIA measurements from northern-hardwood forest types. Among the 1,072 eligible forest areas with larger sugar-maple trees, survey crews recorded maple seedlings in 81.9% of areas with maple saplings and 54.3% of areas without them. After accounting for other measured stand and county characteristics, sapling presence remained the clearest signal that seedlings would also be recorded. The amount of larger sugar maple alone was inconclusive once the sapling stage was considered separately. A model tested on entirely held-out counties captured a useful but imperfect broad pattern (Brier score 0.177; ROC AUC 0.749). These are associations observed at one measurement, not statewide estimates, changes through time, or proof that management, climate, or competition caused the differences.

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
1 Research question
Northern hardwood forests can retain large sugar-maple trees even when younger generations are sparse. Here, “saplings” are young trees 1–4.9 inches in diameter, while “larger trees” are at least 5 inches in diameter. The analysis therefore asks:

Among surveyed Michigan northern-hardwood areas that already contain larger sugar-maple trees, what characteristics distinguish places where crews recorded maple seedlings from places where they recorded none?

This is a snapshot of which size classes occur together. It does not follow individual seedlings as they grow into saplings or mature trees.

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
2 Data and population



2.1 Forest Inventory and Analysis
The Michigan SQLite release comes from the U.S. Forest Service FIA DataMart (U.S. Forest Service 2026). The release pins the current EXPCURR evaluation “MICHIGAN 2025: 2019-2025: CURRENT AREA, CURRENT VOLUME” (EVALID 262501; inventory window 2019–2025). FIA reference tables resolve sugar maple and retained forest types rather than relying on unexplained numeric codes (Burrill et al. 2025).
The analytical key is a plot visit and condition (PLT_CN + CONDID). TREE and SEEDLING records are aggregated independently before joining, which prevents a tree-by-seedling Cartesian product.



2.2 Climate and geography
Daymet Version 4 R1 supplies 1991–2020 temperature and precipitation normals (Thornton et al. 2022). Each county uses one interior representative Daymet cell. These are broad county proxies, not plot exposures.
Exact FIA plot locations are confidential. The analysis neither uses nor infers them. County identifiers are the only spatial link, so the maps show aggregated sample support and no plot-level spatial residual claim is made.




2.3 Cohort construction

The remaining 503 had no sugar-maple TREE record from 1–4.9 inches.

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
3 Methods

3.1 Size classes and basal area
For every live TREE record, plot-basis basal-area contribution is
\[
BA_i = 0.005454 \times DIA_i^2 \times TPA_{i,unadj}.
\]
Condition density is then constructed record by record using the proportion for that record’s sampling frame:
\[
BA_c = \sum_{i \in c}\frac{0.005454 \times DIA_i^2 \times TPA_{i,unadj}}
{PROP_{c,frame(i),unadj}}.
\]
Trees below 5 inches use MICRPROP_UNADJ; trees at least 5 inches use SUBPPROP_UNADJ; MACRPROP_UNADJ is used only when a populated macroplot breakpoint applies. This matches the FIA inventory size-class structure (Burrill et al. 2025). The primary established-tree exposure sums live sugar-maple records with DBH ≥ 5 inches. A separate indicator records whether any live sugar-maple TREE record has DBH 1–4.9 inches. Non-maple basal area remains a competitor covariate and does not treat sugar-maple saplings as non-maple competition.
The calculation is independently checked against FIA COND.BALIVE. Across 1,457 conditions, derived live-tree basal area had Pearson r = 1.000000, mean absolute error 0.000132 ft²/acre, and maximum absolute error 0.000697 ft²/acre.


3.2 Outcome and descriptive screen
The primary response is one when no sugar-maple seedlings were tallied and zero when at least one was tallied. A zero tally is a sampled non-detection, not proof of ecological absence across the condition.
Separately, a transparent descriptive flag identifies sampled conditions with no seedlings tallied and established sugar-maple share in the sample’s upper third. The denominator for that share uses only live trees with DBH ≥ 5 inches. The rule flagged 131 conditions at a cutoff of 51.7%. Because the cutoff is sample-relative, the flag is a screening device and is never used to select the model cohort.


3.3 Primary statistical model
The primary model is a mixed-effects logistic regression with a county random intercept:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{logit}\{P(Y_c=1)\} =\;& \beta_0
+ \beta_1 z\{\log(1 + BA^{est}_{maple,c})\}
+ \beta_2 SaplingPresent_c \\
&+ \beta_3 z\{\log(1 + BA_{nonmaple,c})\}
+ \beta_4 z(MicroplotCoverage_c)
+ \beta_5 Treated_c \\
&+ \beta_6 z(StandAge_c)
+ \beta_7 Disturbed_c
+ \beta_8 z(Temperature_c) \\
&+ \beta_9 z(Precipitation_c)
+ \beta_{10}z(Year_c)
+ u_{county[c]}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Continuous predictors are standardized within the final model-complete cohort. The established-tree term is linear on the standardized log1p scale. A two-degree-of-freedom natural spline did not improve fit (likelihood-ratio p = 0.514; ΔAIC = 1.57). Binary sapling presence had the best AIC among no sapling term, continuous sapling basal area, presence, and presence-plus-amount alternatives. Its likelihood-ratio comparison with no sapling term gave p 4.2e-12.
The county-only random structure was retained. The added plot-visit variance was 0.0000, the extended model was singular, and its AIC was 2.0 points higher. The primary fit has 33.3 outcome events per non-intercept fixed coefficient.

3.4 Validation and robustness
Ten deterministic folds assign whole counties, not individual records. Transformations are learned again within every training fold. Held-out counties are predicted using fixed effects only, so no county random effect leaks into assessment predictions. Performance is summarized with Brier score, ROC AUC, calibration intercept, and calibration slope.
Model-based Wald intervals are accompanied by a fixed-effect logistic sensitivity with county-cluster CR1 covariance. Forest type is evaluated through an omnibus adjustment and a restriction to the dominant type 801. Simulation-based DHARMa checks assess uniformity, dispersion, outliers, and residual quantiles. Recorded treatment is included because it is scientifically motivated and complete, but it is interpreted only as an observational covariate.

Seedlings recorded

with versus without sugar-maple saplings, before accounting for other differences.


Larger trees alone
No clear link
Having more large sugar maple did not clearly indicate whether seedlings would be recorded.

sampled areas combined a high share of larger sugar maple with no seedlings recorded.


Recorded management
A promising lead
This pattern suggests a follow-up question, not proof that management caused better regeneration.



4.1 Study context











(a) Analyzed plot-condition measurements by county. Aggregation protects FIA locations.













(b) Species shares of all live-tree basal-area contribution in the analyzed sample.







Figure 1: Geographic coverage and sampled live-tree composition. Both panels are descriptive sample summaries, not design-based statewide estimates.





4.2 Where larger maple is abundant but seedlings are missing








Figure 2: Established sugar-maple share versus observed seedling density. Positive tallies are plotted exactly in the upper panel. True zero tallies are counted in five-percentage-point bins below, preventing 609 overlapping zeros from appearing as a single row of points. Burgundy bars meet the exploratory upper-third gap rule.





Survey crews recorded no sugar-maple seedlings in 131 of 1,424 sampled forest areas that also had a high share of larger sugar maple. That is 9.2%, or approximately 1 in 11 areas. These are useful places for closer follow-up, but the flag does not prove that regeneration has failed. A stricter definition reduced the count to 102 (7.2%), showing that the total depends on where the screening threshold is set.


4.3 Seedlings and saplings occur together

Seedlings were recorded in 81.9% of areas with sugar-maple saplings, compared with 54.3% of areas without them. Seedlings and saplings were measured at the same visit, so this is evidence that the two life stages occur together, not proof that observed seedlings later grew into saplings.


4.4 What remained after accounting for other differences








Figure 3: Primary and baseline model profiles. The primary panel separates sugar-maple sapling presence from established-tree basal area and displays observed predictor support as rugs. The lower panel retains the all-size nonlinear baseline only to expose the conflation created by mixing saplings and established trees. Curves use cohort-specific reference profiles and are not a formal comparison between models.





At a representative level of larger sugar-maple abundance, the model estimated that crews would record seedlings in 79% of areas with saplings, compared with 55% without saplings. The large separation between the lines shows the sapling signal. Their gentle slopes show that adding more large sugar maple did not clearly change the chance of recording seedlings.

After accounting for the other measured stand and county differences, the main conclusion did not change: areas with sugar-maple saplings were much less likely to have zero seedlings recorded. By contrast, the amount of larger sugar maple remained inconclusive. Areas with more non-maple trees were more likely to have no maple seedlings recorded, although this association does not prove that competition caused the pattern. Sampling coverage also mattered: crews were more likely to encounter seedlings when more of the forest area was represented by sampled microplots.
Areas with a recorded management treatment were also less likely to have zero seedlings recorded. Treatment was flagged in 151 of the 1,072 areas in the primary analysis, and most of those records were broadly classified as cutting. Because this label combines different practices and the same places were not compared before and after treatment, the result is a lead for future research, not evidence that cutting improved regeneration.
In this sample, warmer counties were more likely to have no seedlings recorded after the other measured differences were considered, while the precipitation result was inconclusive. The climate values are broad county averages, so they provide geographic context rather than evidence of a plot-level climate effect.

The binary sapling term outperformed a continuous amount term. Adding positive sapling amount after presence increased AIC by 1.50, so the simpler ecological indicator was retained.
The county-cluster CR1 sensitivity gave a sapling-presence OR of 0.30 (95% CI 0.20–0.44). Forest-type indicators did not improve the primary model in an omnibus test (p = 0.545). Restricting to the dominant type 801 left the established-tree direction similar but imprecise (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.74–1.18). Sparse forest-type cells are not interpreted individually.


4.6 Model adequacy
The model separated seedling-recorded areas from zero-seedling areas reasonably well when tested on counties that were completely excluded during fitting. That supports the broad pattern, but the model is not accurate enough to predict the outcome of an individual forest stand.

No simulation-based check crossed the pre-specified 0.05 flag: uniformity p = 0.219, dispersion p = 0.800, outlier p = 1.000, and combined residual-quantile p = 0.523. Passing diagnostics do not prove that the model is perfectly specified.


4.7 Broad geographic pattern








Figure 5: Exploratory gap fraction among seedling-sampled conditions. Gray counties had fewer than 20 eligible conditions or no data. This is a descriptive sample map, not a design-based county estimate.

Only 17 counties had at least 20 seedling-sampled areas, the minimum used for display. The apparent differences should not be treated as county rankings because uncertainty is wide and the summaries are not formal statewide estimates. Counties with less information are shown in gray rather than assigned unstable percentages. Because public FIA data identify only the county, this project does not claim to test fine-scale spatial patterns at actual plot locations.

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
5 Discussion


What the evidence supports

Where larger sugar maples already grow, finding saplings is the clearest sign that seedlings are also being recorded.
More large sugar maples alone did not clearly indicate whether seedlings were present.
Other trees, sampling coverage, recorded management, and broad climate patterns added secondary clues.
The main pattern remained useful when the model was tested on counties it had not seen before.



What it does not establish

Which seedlings will survive to become saplings or mature trees.
That management, climate, canopy, browsing, or competition caused the observed differences.
How common these patterns are across every Michigan forest.
Precise local patterns at confidential FIA plot locations.



The most important ecological message is that a mature sugar-maple canopy does not, by itself, demonstrate renewal. An initial analysis appeared to show a strong relationship between total sugar-maple abundance and seedlings, but that measure mixed young saplings with larger trees. Separating the life stages changed the story: sapling presence, not simply having more mature maple, was the clearest sign that seedlings were also present.
For forest resilience, the practical insight is straightforward: look beyond the canopy and check whether both seedlings and saplings are present. A next study should revisit the same places through time to learn which seedlings survive, while also measuring browsing, soils, competing vegetation, and the timing and type of management.

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
6 Limitations

Cross-sectional outcome. Size classes are observed at one measurement, so arrows in the conceptual story do not represent observed transitions.
Sampling opportunity. A zero means no seedlings were tallied on sampled microplots, not absence across the entire condition.
Observational treatment. TRTCD records heterogeneous recent treatments and supplies no randomized or before-and-after counterfactual.
Sample versus population. TPA_UNADJ and frame proportions expand records within the plot design; they are not statewide survey weights. Formal estimates require FIA evaluation, stratum, adjustment, and sampling-error procedures (Bechtold and Patterson 2005).
Broad climate proxies. One county interior Daymet cell cannot reproduce plot-level climate or recent weather.
Confidential locations. County aggregation protects plots but prevents fine-scale spatial analysis.
Unmeasured drivers. Browsing, soils, seed supply, competing vegetation, and treatment detail remain incomplete.
Exploratory gap flag. The upper-third rule is sample-relative and threshold-dependent.

7 Reproducibility


85
hashed source artifacts


83
county Daymet responses


10
county-held-out folds


renv
locked R environment


Raw FIA data are excluded from version control. The public repository records source URLs, retrieval timestamps, file sizes, and SHA-256 checksums for cached inputs. Join audits record row counts, unique keys, and unmatched keys. Model artifacts include cohort support, scaling constants, functional-form and random-structure comparisons, conventional and county-cluster inference, forest-type sensitivity, validation folds, diagnostics, and the exact data behind the published curves.
From a fresh clone, the analysis runs with:
make setup
make acquire
make all
Package versions are recorded in renv.lock. The release was tested with R 4.6.1 and Quarto 1.9.38. FIA’s state archive URL is mutable, so acquisition checks source size and SHA-256 against the published manifest before analysis.

02 · Define

Build the cohort
6,459 assigned visits narrow to 1,457 conditions in FIA’s maple/beech/birch forest-type group, used as the operational northern-hardwood cohort.



03 · Integrate

Preserve geography
83 county Daymet cells join by GEOID. Exact FIA plot locations are confidential; public coordinates may be approximate, and this analysis neither uses nor infers them.



04 · Estimate

Model clustering
1,072 outcomes support a county random intercept, an established-tree term, and a separate sapling-stage indicator.



05 · Validate

Publish evidence
County-held-out validation (Brier 0.177; AUC 0.749), join audits, source hashes, diagnostics, functional-form comparisons, and sensitivity analyses accompany the report.




Technical reviewer? Inspect the data dictionary · Trace analysis decisions · Review the source and validation evidence

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
What the analysis found
Within the established-tree cohort, raw seedling non-detection was 45.7% without sugar-maple saplings and 18.1% with them. After adjustment, sapling presence was associated with 67% lower odds of a zero seedling tally (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.24–0.45).
That is a cross-sectional association, not a transition or causal effect. A seedling zero means “not tallied” rather than confirmed ecological absence, and county climate values are broad proxies.



Built for auditability

FIA species and forest types resolve from reference tables.
Trees and seedlings aggregate before joining.
Sampling opportunity controls whether a missing seedling record can become zero.
Checksums, join audits, support gates, and tests travel with the analysis.




Spatially responsible
Exact FIA plot locations are confidential. The analysis neither uses nor infers public plot coordinates; maps and climate joins use county identifiers, and sparse county summaries are suppressed.

title: Canopy to Cohort
text:
Research artifact
The report documents the pinned 2025 current evaluation (inventory window 2019–2025; assigned measurement records 2018–2025), cohort construction, size-class correction, equations, model support, sensitivity analysis, limitations, and reproducibility workflow.
Open the complete report →
Code

Pre-specified boundaries

The analytical key is one plot visit and condition: PLT_CN + CONDID.
The response is whether sugar-maple seedlings were tallied on sampled microplots. Its inverse is “no seedlings tallied,” not confirmed absence.
The regeneration-gap flag is a descriptive screen, not a validated index or the regression response.
Climate is a county-scale proxy and cannot be interpreted as plot exposure.
Maps summarize the analyzed sample, not design-based county or statewide population estimates.
Exact FIA plot locations are neither used nor inferred.
Longitudinal transition analysis and formal FIA population estimation remain future extensions.

Source and cohort

FIADB source. Michigan’s SQLite FIADB archive was retrieved from the FIA DataMart. The acquisition audit records the URL, byte size, retrieval time, and SHA-256 checksum.
Evaluation. Release v1.3.0 pins EVALID 262501, “MICHIGAN 2025: 2019-2025: CURRENT AREA, CURRENT VOLUME.” The evaluation inventory window is 2019–2025; assigned measurement records span 2018–2025. A configuration change is required to analyze a different evaluation.
Operational northern-hardwood cohort. FIA forest-type group 800 is the maple / beech / birch group. Active retained types resolve from REF_FOREST_TYPE: 801 sugar maple / beech / yellow birch, 802 black cherry, 805 hard maple / basswood, and 809 red maple / upland.
Sugar maple. REF_SPECIES resolves Acer saccharum to SPCD 318.
Seedling opportunity. A condition is sampled only when MICRPROP_UNADJ > 0. An absent sugar-maple SEEDLING row becomes zero only under that demonstrated opportunity.

Size-class correction
The v1.3.0 scientific model separates FIA TREE size classes instead of treating all live sugar-maple basal area as established canopy structure.

Established-tree cohort. The primary cohort requires at least one live sugar-maple TREE record with DBH ≥ 5 inches, FIA’s subplot-tree threshold. This rule is inventory-defined, independent of the seedling outcome, and retains 1,072 sampled conditions in 66 counties.
Sapling stage. Sugar-maple sapling presence means at least one live TREE record with DBH 1–4.9 inches. Presence is kept separate from established-tree basal area.
Competitor basal area. The model uses live non-maple basal area. It does not subtract established sugar maple from total basal area because that would misclassify sugar-maple saplings as competitors.
Basal-area frames. Each live-tree plot-basis contribution is 0.005454 * DIA^2 * TPA_UNADJ. Condition density uses MICRPROP_UNADJ for microplot trees, SUBPPROP_UNADJ for subplot trees, and MACRPROP_UNADJ only above an applicable populated macroplot breakpoint. Derived total live basal area must pass strict agreement gates against COND.BALIVE.

The previous full-cohort model is retained as an explicitly labeled baseline. Its nonlinear curve mixes 1–4.9-inch sugar-maple saplings into its basal-area predictor and includes conditions without established sugar maple. It therefore mixes species absence with regeneration continuity and is not the primary model.

Primary model

Response. outcome_no_seedlings = 1 - maple_seedling_detected.
Fixed effects. Standardized log1p established sugar-maple basal area, sugar-maple sapling presence, standardized log1p non-maple basal area, microplot condition coverage, recorded treatment, stand age, disturbance, county temperature and precipitation proxies, and measurement year.
Functional form. A linear standardized log1p established-tree term is selected. A two-degree-of-freedom spline did not improve fit. Binary sapling presence had lower AIC than no sapling term, continuous sapling basal area, or presence plus positive sapling amount.
Treatment. The FIA treatment indicator is included because it is complete, scientifically relevant, and supported by 151 primary-cohort observations. It remains observational and is never described as a management effect.
Grouping. County GEOID is the retained random intercept. Adding a plot visit intercept produced zero estimated variance, a singular fit, and no AIC improvement.
Inference. Conventional fixed-effect summaries use model-based Wald 95% intervals. A fixed-effect logistic model with county-cluster CR1 covariance is reported as sensitivity evidence.
Validation. Ten deterministic folds hold out whole counties. Every fold relearns transformations from training data and predicts held-out counties with fixed effects only. This is internal geographic validation, not external validation.
Forest type. Indicators are evaluated through an omnibus sensitivity; the dominant type 801 is also refit alone. Sparse type cells are not interpreted individually.
Diagnostics. DHARMa checks cover uniformity, dispersion, outliers, and residual quantiles. A county-plus-plot random-structure comparison and collinearity audit are published.

Descriptive gap screen
The high-established threshold is the upper third of frame-corrected established sugar-maple basal-area share among seedling-sampled conditions. The share denominator includes only live trees with DBH ≥ 5 inches. An upper-quartile alternative is reported. The sample-relative threshold is never reused to construct the inferential cohort.

Spatial decision
The Daymet normal uses the cell at each Census Gazetteer county internal point. It is a county proxy, not a county-wide areal mean. Plot-level residual spatial autocorrelation cannot be tested without plot coordinates. A naïve test on county-aggregated residuals was rejected because it is unstable and does not represent plot-scale dependence.
